body.text: After setting up an applied optimization problem, the next step is to solve. To solve the applied optimization problem, find the global maximum or minimum of the objective function.
In many cases, the domain is a closed interval. To find global extrema on a closed interval:

items: Identify critical numbers by finding where the derivative is \(0\) or undefined.
Evaluate the function at the critical numbers and the endpoints of the interval.
Compare the function values to determine the global maximum or minimum.

body.text: In an earlier example, an architect wanted to maximize the area of a rectangular window enclosed by \(16\text{ feet}\) of framing using an objective function \(A(x) = x(8-x)\) on the domain \([0, 8].\) This optimization problem can now be solved by finding the global maximum on this closed interval.
This lesson will demonstrate how to solve applied optimization problems.

sections.transcript: We want to find the maximum area of a rectangular window using 16 feet of window frame. We have already completed the first five steps as part of the setup in the previous lesson. We found an objective function A of x with a domain from 0 to 8. To solve, we now find the global maximum using the process for finding global extrema of a differentiable function on a closed interval. We start with the derivative of A of x, which is A prime of x equals 8 minus 2 x. Now we set the derivative equal to 0 to find any critical numbers. The only critical number is x equals 4. To find the maximum on a closed interval, we compare the function values at the endpoints of the interval and the critical numbers. Substituting the first endpoint 0 into the factored form of the area function gives A of 0 equals 0 times open paren 8 minus 0 close paren, which is 0. Substituting the other endpoint 8 into A of x also gives 0. Substituting the critical number into the area function gives A of 4 equals 16. Comparing the three function values, we find that the largest is 16 when x equals 4. So the maximum area of the window is 16 square feet. This maximum occurs when one side of the window frame is 4 feet long, and the other side is 8 minus 4 feet long.

questions.prompt: When setting the derivative \(A^\prime(x) = 8 - 2x\) equal to \(0,\) the only critical number is \(\underline{\phantom{XXXXXX}}.\)
hints: Solve \(8 - 2x = 0\) for \(x.\)
Add \(2x\) to both sides of the equation, then divide by \(2.\)
questions.correctExplanation: Setting \(A^\prime(x)\) equal to \(0\) and solving for \(x,\) \[\begin{align*} A^\prime(x) = 8 - 2x &= 0 \\ 8 &= 2x && \text{Add} \\ 4 &= x && \text{Divide} \end{align*}\] \(x = 4.\)

questions.prompt: Substituting the critical number \(x = 4\) into \(A(x) = x(8 - x)\) gives \(\underline{\phantom{XXXXXX}}.\)
hints: Substituting \(x = 4\) gives \(A(4) = 4(8 - 4).\)
Simplify \(4(8 - 4).\)

body.text: In the autumn, salmon swim upstream to spawn on gravel beds in small creeks. For one population of salmon, the number \(S\) of salmon swimming upstream is approximated by the function
where \(T\) is the temperature of the water in degrees Celsius and \(5 \leq T \leq 20.\)
Find the water temperature that produces the maximum number of salmon swimming upstream.

questions.prompt: The only critical number of \(S(T)\) is \(\underline{\phantom{XXXXXX}}.\)
hints: Take the derivative of \(S(T),\) then set \(S^\prime(T)\) equal to \(0.\)
Solve \(S^\prime(T) = -2T + 20 = 0\) for \(T.\)
questions.correctExplanation: Taking the derivative of \(S(T) = -T^2 + 20T + 1000\) gives \(S^\prime(T) = -2T + 20.\) Setting the derivative equal to zero and solving, \[\begin{align*}S^\prime(T) = -2T + 20 & = 0 \\20 & = 2T \\10 & = T \end{align*}\] So the only critical number is \(T = 10.\)

questions.prompt: Values of the objective function \(S(T)\) computed at the endpoints of the domain and the critical number are given in the table. \(T\) \(S(T)\) \(5\) \(-(5)^2+20(5) + 1000 = 1075 \) \(20\) \(-(20)^2 + 20(20) + 1000= 1000\) \(10\) \(-(10)^2+20(10)+1000=1100\) The water temperature that produces the maximum number of salmon swimming upstream is \(\underline{\phantom{XXXXXX}}.\)
hints: Compare the three function values in the table, and find the \(T\text{-}\) value corresponding to the largest function value.
The maximum number of salmon is \(1100.\) Find the \(T\text{-}\) value in the table corresponding to \(1100\) salmon.
questions.correctExplanation: Comparing the function values \(S(5) = 1075,\) \(S(20) = 1000,\) and \(S(10) = 1100,\) reveals that \(1100\) is the largest. So the maximum number of salmon swimming upstream is \(1100,\) and this maximum occurs when the temperature of the water is \(T = 10 ^{\circ} \text{C}.\)

body.text: Solve the area problem with a rectangular window and \(3\) window panes, which was set up in the previous lesson. An architect has \(40\text{ feet}\) of window framing and wants to build a rectangular window with \(3\) parallel window panes separated by framing as in the figure.

The area is given by \(A(x) = x(20 -2x)= 20x - 2x^2,\) where \(x\) is the length of the of each of the \(4\) parallel pieces of window framing. Find the maximum area of the window on the interval \([0, 10].\)

questions.prompt: Find the global maximum of the objective function \(A(x) = 20x - 2x^2\) on the closed interval \([0, 10].\) The first step is to find the critical numbers of the objective function. The only critical number of \(A(x) = 20x - 2x^2\) is \(x=\underline{\phantom{XXXXXX}}.\)

choices.explanation: The derivative of \(A(x)\) is \(A^\prime(x) = 20 - 4x.\) Substituting \(0\) into \(A^\prime(x)\) gives \(A^\prime(0) = 20 - 4(0) =20.\) The derivative is defined and is not \(0\) at \(x = 0,\) so \(x = 0\) is not a critical number.

To find critical numbers, use the derivative equal to \(0.\) The derivative of \(A(x)\) is \(A^\prime(x) = 20 - 4x\) by the constant multiple and power rules. Setting \(A^\prime(x)\) equal to \(0\) and solving, \[\begin{align*}A^\prime(x) = 20 - 4x & = 0 \\20 & = 4x \\ 5 & = x\end{align*}\] So the only critical number is \(x =5.\)

The derivative of \(A(x)\) is \(A^\prime(x) = 20 - 4x.\) Substituting \(10\) into \(A^\prime(x)\) gives \(A^\prime(10) = 20 - 4(10) =-20.\) The derivative is defined and is not \(0\) at \(x = 10,\) so \(x = 10\) is not a critical number.

hints: Compare the \(3\) function values in the table.
The maximum area is the largest function value from the table.
questions.correctExplanation: Comparing the function values \(A(0) = 0,\) \(A(10) = 0,\) and \(A(5) = 50,\) reveals that \(50\) is the largest. So the maximum area of the window is \(50 \text{ sq. ft.}\)

questions.prompt: Values of the objective function computed at the endpoints of the domain and the critical number are given in the table. \(x\) \(A(x)\) \(0\) \(0(20 - 2(0)) = 0\) \(10\) \(10(20 -2(10)) = 0\) \(5\) \(5(20 - 2(5))=50\) The maximum area of the window is \(50 \text{ sq. ft.},\) which corresponds to where the \(4\) parallel pieces of window frame each have a length of \(\underline{\phantom{XXXXXX}}.\)
hints: Find the \(x\text{-}\) value corresponding to the maximum.
Find the \(x\text{-}\) value in the first column of the table corresponding to the function value \(50.\)
questions.correctExplanation: The maximum area is \(A(5) = 50,\) which corresponds to \(x = 5.\) So the length of each the \(4\) parallel pieces of window framing that gives the maximum area is \(5 \text{ ft.}\)

body.text: Solve the area problem with a rectangular backyard, which was set up in the previous lesson. A farmer has \(80\text{ feet}\) of material to fence \(3\) sides of a rectangular backyard.
The area is given by \(A(x) = 80x - 2x^2 = x(80 -2x)\text{,}\) where \(x\) is the length of the backyard. Find the maximum area of the backyard on the interval \([0, 40].\)

questions.prompt: Find the global maximum of the objective function \(A(x) = 80x - 2x^2\) on the closed interval \([0, 40]\text{.}\) The first step is to find the critical numbers of the objective function. The only critical number of \(A(x) = 80x - 2x^2\) is \( \underline{\phantom{XXXXXX}}.\)
hints: Find the derivative \(A^\prime(x),\) then solve \(A'(x) = 0\) to find the critical numbers.
The derivative is \(A'(x) = 80 - 4x.\)
questions.correctExplanation: Taking the derivative of \(A(x) = 80x - 2x^2\) using the constant multiple and power rules, \(A^\prime(x)= 80 - 4x.\) Setting this derivative equal to \(0\) and solving, \[\begin{align*} A'(x) = 80 - 4x & = 0 \\ -4x &= -80 \\ x &= 20 \end{align*}\] \(x = 20.\)

questions.prompt: The only critical number, \(x = 20,\) lies inside the domain \([0, 40].\) Next, evaluate the objective function at the endpoints of the domain and the critical number. The results of evaluating the function at the endpoints of the interval \([0,40]\) are given in the table. \(x\) \(A(x)\) \(0\) \(0(80 - 2(0)) = 0\) \(40\) \(40(80 -2(40)) = 0\) \(20\) \(?\) Substituting the critical number \(x = 20\) into \(A(x) = 80x - 2x^2 = x(80-2x)\) gives \( \underline{\phantom{XXXXXX}}.\)
hints: Substitute \(x = 20\) into \(A(x) = x(80-2x).\)
Substituting gives \(A(20) = 20(80 - 2(20)).\)
questions.correctExplanation: Substituting \(20\) into \(A(x) = x(80 -2x)\) and simplifying, \[\begin{align*} A(x) &= x(80-2x) \\ A(20) &= 20(80 - 2(20)) \\ & = 20(40) \\ &= 800 & \\ \end{align*}\]

questions.prompt: Find the solution of this optimization problem based on the values of the objective function computed at the endpoints of the domain and the critical number. \(x\) \(A(x)\) \(0\) \(0(80 - 2(0)) = 0\) \(40\) \(40(80 -2(40)) = 0\) \(20\) \(20(80 - 2(20))=800\) The maximum area of the backyard is \(\underline{\phantom{XXXXXX}}.\)
hints: Compare the \(3\) function values in the table.
The maximum area is the largest function value in the table.
questions.correctExplanation: Comparing the function values \(A(0) = 0,\) \(A(40) = 0,\) and \(A(20) = 800\) reveals that \(800\) is the largest. So the maximum area of the backyard is \(800 \text{ sq. ft.}\)

questions.prompt: Find the solution of this optimization problem based on the values of the objective function computed at the endpoints of the domain and the critical number. \(x\) \(A(x)\) \(0\) \(0(80 - 2(0)) = 0\) \(40\) \(40(80 -2(40)) = 0\) \(20\) \(40(80 - 2(20)) = 800\) The maximum area of the backyard is \(800 \text{ sq. ft.},\) which corresponds to a backyard with a length of \(\underline{\phantom{XXXXXX}}.\)
hints: Find the \(x\text{-}\) value corresponding to the maximum.
Find the \(x\text{-}\) value in the first column of the table corresponding to the function value \(800.\)
questions.correctExplanation: The maximum area is \(A(20) = 800,\) which corresponds to \(x = 20.\) So the backyard length that gives the maximum area is \(20 \text{ ft.}\)
